text_blocks.snippet: There are two main types of stroke: ischemic and hemorrhagic. Ischemic strokes, the most common, are caused by a blockage in a blood vessel, while hemorrhagic strokes are caused by bleeding in the brain.

list.snippet: Thrombotic: A blood clot forms in a blood vessel in the brain, often due to atherosclerosis (plaque buildup).
Embolic: A blood clot travels from another part of the body (often the heart) and lodges in a brain artery.
Small vessel occlusion (lacunar stroke): A blockage in a small artery deep within the brain.
